name: Xenia and Colorful Gems
description: Xenia is a girl being born a noble. Due to the inflexibility and harshness of her family, Xenia has to find some ways to amuse herself. Recently Xenia has bought $$$n_r$$$ red gems, $$$n_g$$$ green gems and $$$n_b$$$ blue gems. Each of the gems has a weight. Now, she is going to pick three gems. Xenia loves colorful things, so she will pick exactly one gem of each color. Xenia loves balance, so she will try to pick gems with little difference in weight. Specifically, supposing the weights of the picked gems are $$$x$$$, $$$y$$$ and $$$z$$$, Xenia wants to find the minimum value of $$$(x-y)^2+(y-z)^2+(z-x)^2$$$. As her dear friend, can you help her?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t \le 100$$$)  — the number of test cases. Then $$$t$$$ test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n_r,n_g,n_b$$$ ($$$1\le n_r,n_g,n_b\le 10^5$$$)  — the number of red gems, green gems and blue gems respectively. The second line of each test case contains $$$n_r$$$ integers $$$r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_{n_r}$$$ ($$$1\le r_i \le 10^9$$$)  — $$$r_i$$$ is the weight of the $$$i$$$-th red gem. The third line of each test case contains $$$n_g$$$ integers $$$g_1,g_2,\ldots,g_{n_g}$$$ ($$$1\le g_i \le 10^9$$$)  — $$$g_i$$$ is the weight of the $$$i$$$-th green gem. The fourth line of each test case contains $$$n_b$$$ integers $$$b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_{n_b}$$$ ($$$1\le b_i \le 10^9$$$)  — $$$b_i$$$ is the weight of the $$$i$$$-th blue gem. It is guaranteed that $$$\sum n_r \le 10^5$$$, $$$\sum n_g \le 10^5$$$, $$$\sum n_b \le 10^5$$$ (the sum for all test cases).
output_specification: For each test case, print a line contains one integer  — the minimum value which Xenia wants to find.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1336B — Xenia and Colorful Gems [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
